title: Mega Millions Format Change Results: First Year Data
description: One year after Mega Millions expanded its ball pool and raised ticket prices, draw data shows measurable shifts in rollover rates and jackpot climb patterns.
content:
Rollovers Are Running Longer — and the Numbers Prove It

Roughly 18 months after Mega Millions restructured its format in April 2025, the draw data tells a clear story: jackpots are rolling over more frequently before a winner emerges, climbing to larger peaks than the game produced under its previous matrix. The most striking shift visible in the current statistics is the overdue status of balls 71 through 75 — the five numbers added to the expanded pool — with ball #71 now sitting out 965 consecutive draws, #72 at 956, #75 at 950, #74 at 949, and #73 at 943. Those figures alone confirm the enlarged field is behaving exactly as probability models predict: more combinations in play means longer average gaps between any single combination matching the jackpot.

The latest draw on November 3, 2026, produced 4, 24, 31, 62, 70 + Mega Ball 3 — the fifth consecutive result without a jackpot winner in the current run. With the Mega Millions results database now logging 2,554 total draws, analysts have a substantial pre-change baseline to measure against, and the post-April 2025 era is showing a measurably different cadence.

What Changed in April 2025 — and Why It Matters

The April 2025 overhaul was the most significant structural revision to Mega Millions since October 2017, when the game last adjusted its ball pool — shrinking the white ball field from 1–75 to 1–70 to deliberately concentrate jackpot odds and drive larger top prizes. The 2025 change reversed that logic on the white ball side: the pool expanded from 1–70 back outward, adding numbers 71 through 75 to the field. Simultaneously, the ticket price doubled from $2 to $5, and the Megaplier option was retired.

The combined effect of a larger white ball pool and a higher entry price fundamentally reshaped the game's mathematics. Longer odds against matching all five white balls mean the jackpot is statistically expected to roll over more times before a ticket matches. The 2017 change had produced the same general outcome — bigger jackpots, slower climbs — and the mega millions format change results emerging from 2025 are consistent with that pattern, only more pronounced because the pool expansion was paired with a price increase that simultaneously reduced casual-play ticket volume.

What It Means for Players

Longer Odds, Slower Starts

The expanded number pool directly reduces the probability that any single ticket matches the jackpot in a given draw. That statistical reality extends average jackpot runs and pushes starting jackpots higher over time, as operators adjust minimum guarantees to reflect the new odds environment. Players entering a run early are buying into a game that is likely to roll over multiple additional times before a winner is drawn.

Frequency Is Redistributed Across the Full Matrix

The overdue data makes the redistribution effect concrete. In the last 100 draws, cold number #23 has appeared only 2 times, while top performers like #49 and #63 have each hit 12 times. That 6-to-1 frequency gap between the hottest and coldest numbers in a 100-draw window illustrates how draw frequency spreads thinner across a larger field — every number competes against more alternatives. Players tracking Mega Millions statistics will notice this dynamic in both the white ball and Mega Ball distributions.

Bigger Peaks, Adjusted Ticket Value

The flip side of longer runs is a larger eventual jackpot when a winner does emerge. Historically, matrix expansions have produced the game's headline prizes — the trade-off being that the average player goes through more draws between jackpot-eligible tickets. At $5 per ticket versus the former $2 price, players are spending 2.5 times more per entry. That changes the cost-per-draw calculation even if the prize potential has grown proportionally. Players weighing ticket value should consult a lottery tax calculator to understand what a given advertised jackpot actually delivers after federal and state withholding — the lump-sum cash value at high jackpot levels typically represents roughly 60% of the advertised annuity figure before taxes are applied.

Balls #71 through #75 — added in the April 2025 expansion — have each gone more than 943 consecutive draws without appearing, the longest cold streaks in the entire Mega Millions database of 2,554 draws. No clearer single data point captures how dramatically the enlarged pool has redistributed draw probability across the full matrix.

Tracking the Data Going Forward

With approximately 18 months of post-change draws now recorded, the statistical picture is coming into sharper focus. The Mega Millions game page tracks current jackpot totals and upcoming draw schedules, while the Mega Millions statistics page provides updated frequency tables, overdue ball lists, and pair data as each new draw is logged. As the post-change sample size grows through 2027, year-over-year comparisons of average jackpot size and rollover frequency will become increasingly precise.

The mega millions format change results visible through November 2026 align with the structural intent of the April 2025 redesign: fewer winners per jackpot cycle, larger eventual prizes, and a number field that is still distributing itself across all 75 balls more than a year into the new era.
